newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 index continues to regain lost ground.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 index continues to regain lost ground.

text.p: The Czech RPIX and PX50 indices closed higher on Monday confirming the beginning of a rebound which began towards the end of last week.
The PX50 rose 1.8 points to 534.7 while the RPIX was up two to 1,090.
Major issues were mixed, with CEZ down eight crowns to 1,012, Komercni Banka up 25 crowns to 2,225 and SPT Telecom unchanged on 3,100.
Ceska Sporitelna, the country's biggest savings bank was also unchanged, on 330, despite posting higher nine month net profits of 1.6 billion crowns versus 1.19 billion in the same period in 1995.
Analysts said the figures were in line with expectations and Brno-based brokerage Atlantik Financni Trhy said the share was in any case overpriced.
"I don't think analysts are surprised by these figures. Its still valued by us at about 285 anyway," said Atlantik's Dan Gladis.
Gladis said that his company's assessment of Sporitelna was based on the bank's long term future prospects but he conceded that there were still some buyers in the market.
Elsewhere on the bourse, Investicni Banka - the fourth biggest Czech bank - rose 15 crowns, or five percent, to 316.

On Friday, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said that Investicni was first in line among the big Czech banks for further privatisation, adding that a strong foreign strategic partner would be the most likely beneficiary of any sell off.
Nomura and ING Bank have been mooted in the Czech press as potential buyers.
